title: Impurity count is not electrical impact
caption: Unwanted impurities and deliberate dopants both occur in small quantities, but their electrical roles differ. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Ideal silicon lattice
nodes.detail: A regular bonding network provides the starting material.

nodes.label: Intentional dopants
nodes.detail: Selected atoms create controlled carrier populations.

nodes.label: Unwanted impurities
nodes.detail: Other atoms can change resistivity or introduce traps.

source.heading: 1. Why Purity Is the Whole Game

title: The furnace needs a permeable charge
caption: Selected lump quartz and carbon form a bed through which reaction gas can escape; loose beach sand is not equivalent feedstock. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Selected quartz
nodes.detail: Rock chemistry and mechanical strength matter.

nodes.label: Carbon charge
nodes.detail: Carbon participates in the reduction reaction.

nodes.label: Open gas paths
nodes.detail: The packed bed must allow evolved gas to leave.

title: Break the silicon–oxygen bond with heat and carbon
caption: Electrical energy drives the overall reduction; silicon and gaseous carbon monoxide leave through different paths. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Quartz and carbon
nodes.detail: The charge supplies silicon oxide and reducing carbon.

nodes.label: Submerged-arc furnace
nodes.detail: Electrodes deliver intense heat inside the bed.

nodes.label: Molten silicon
nodes.detail: Reduced silicon collects for tapping.

nodes.label: Reaction gas
nodes.detail: Carbon monoxide escapes through the charge.

title: Purify a volatile intermediate, then rebuild silicon
caption: The Siemens route separates chemical purification from deposition; gas recovery closes the supporting recycle loops. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Make chlorosilanes
nodes.detail: Metallurgical silicon reacts to form volatile compounds.

nodes.label: Distill the feed
nodes.detail: Fractionation separates trace contaminants.

nodes.label: Deposit on hot rods
nodes.detail: Purified feed decomposes to solid silicon.

nodes.label: Recover and recycle
nodes.detail: Chlorine and hydrogen-bearing streams return to the process.

title: A growing bed of silicon granules
caption: Upward gas flow suspends seeds while decomposition adds silicon to their surfaces; product can be withdrawn continuously. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Silane feed
nodes.detail: Purified precursor enters from below.

nodes.label: Fluidized seed bed
nodes.detail: Gas supports particles and exposes their surfaces.

nodes.label: Heated growth region
nodes.detail: Precursor decomposition deposits silicon on seeds.

nodes.label: Granular product
nodes.detail: Larger particles leave as silicon feedstock.

source.heading: 5. FBR Granular Polysilicon: the Silane Route

title: The grade follows the device requirement
caption: Purity labels alone do not capture all quality requirements; electronic and solar buyers qualify different electrical and contamination specifications. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Electronic devices
nodes.detail: Tight contaminant and resistivity control protects circuit behavior.

nodes.label: Solar cells
nodes.detail: Carrier lifetime and photovoltaic performance guide feedstock limits.

nodes.label: Customer qualification
nodes.detail: Measurements establish whether a lot fits its intended process.

source.heading: 6. Grades: Electronic Grade vs Solar Grade

title: Build a purity picture from complementary measurements
caption: No single assay proves every impurity limit; analytical and electrical methods observe different consequences of contamination. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Chemical analysis
nodes.detail: Spectrometry identifies selected trace species.

nodes.label: Optical measurements
nodes.detail: Absorption reveals particular impurities or bonds.

nodes.label: Electrical measurements
nodes.detail: Resistivity and lifetime expose electrical effects.

nodes.label: Qualified polysilicon
nodes.detail: The combined evidence supports a feedstock specification.

title: Charged silicon exceeds shipped wafer mass
caption: Growth scrap, sawing kerf and surface finishing all separate material from the eventual wafer. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Charge the puller
nodes.detail: The starting polysilicon mass enters the melt.

nodes.label: Crop the crystal
nodes.detail: Unusable ends and residual melt reduce output.

nodes.label: Slice the body
nodes.detail: Saw kerf consumes silicon between slices.

nodes.label: Finish the surface
nodes.detail: Grinding, etching and polishing remove more material.

source.heading: 8. How Much Polysilicon a Wafer Needs

title: Capacity and price move on different clocks
caption: A price rise can encourage investment, but new plants arrive later; the figure is a qualitative commodity-cycle mechanism, not a price forecast. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Tight available supply
nodes.detail: Buyers compete for current output.

nodes.label: Investment decisions
nodes.detail: Producers plan additional manufacturing capacity.

nodes.label: New capacity arrives
nodes.detail: Construction and qualification delay the supply response.

nodes.label: Inventory pressure
nodes.detail: Excess output can pressure prices and future investment.

title: The hot zone is another contamination path
caption: The melt contacts a crucible and sits near hot structural materials; purity must extend beyond the silicon charge. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Polysilicon charge
nodes.detail: Provides the silicon being crystallized.

nodes.label: Quartz crucible
nodes.detail: Holds the melt and can contribute oxygen.

nodes.label: Graphite hot zone
nodes.detail: Heats and supports the vessel nearby.

nodes.label: Controlled melt
nodes.detail: All surrounding materials influence the crystal environment.
